rules.on_page: In all 28 'partly' verdicts the crop stopped short of the passage's end because the locator's end match was weak. The part shown was printed on the page in every case, so 'partly' counts as on the page, for the part checked.
rules.one_item: Yes when every printing carries the item the story's title names, even if some printings' matched text runs a little into the next paragraph. No when the shared text is a run of separate items (a digest), or when the story chains items so that some printings do not carry the titled item. Reports of one legislature's sittings printed as one continuing report count as one item.
rules.transcription: Fact-changing (major): a number, date or proper name read as a different plausible one; a word read as a different real word that changes the sense; words, a line, a signature or table data dropped or added. Minor: garbles a reader would recognise as errors, spelling or word-form variants, near-synonyms that keep the sense, silent corrections of printed misprints, and dropped or added small words that do not change the sense.

value.method: The automatic families of 1807 that reach 4 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running), were split into single printed items (items.json: 177 items in 7 or more papers, 31 in 9 or more). Those items were read and the stories chosen by the rule below. Each chosen item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 4,167 pages of 1807 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched by hand with loose keywords. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json); 39 crops were placed by hand where the text-layer locator missed the passage.

value.selection_rule: As for 1776: every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs and items that need careful framing. Items in 7 or 8 papers were chosen to cover the months and the main kinds of news. Stories are counted item by item; where one publication holds several documents (the Norfolk letters of July, the Chesapeake papers, the Burr affair), each document is its own group under a parent story. Every group reaches 7 or more papers. A paper that printed an item again later counts each printing.
